questions.question: The unit of formula unit mass is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms in a formula unit of a compound.
 
• It is calculated in exactly the same manner as the **molecular mass** is calculated; however, the term "formula unit" is used for those substances whose constituent particles are **ions**.
 
• The standard unit for expressing both molecular mass and formula unit mass is the **unified atomic mass unit**, which is represented by the symbol **u**. ***Hence, the correct option is u.***
 
• In the case of ionic compounds like **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, we do not use the term molecule; instead, we use the **formula unit**. The mass of **NaCl** is calculated as (1 x **23 u**) + (1 x **35.5 u**) = **58.5 u**.
 
• Another example is **Calcium Chloride (CaCl2)**. The formula unit mass is calculated by adding the atomic mass of one **Calcium** atom (**40 u**) and two **Chlorine** atoms (2 x **35.5 u**), resulting in a total of **111 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u):**

 
 
• It is defined as a mass unit equal to exactly **one-twelfth (1/12th)** the mass of one atom of **Carbon-12**.
 
• The **relative atomic mass** of the atom of an element is the average mass of the atom, as compared to **1/12th** the mass of one **Carbon-12** atom.
 
• Previously, it was abbreviated as **amu** (atomic mass unit), but according to the latest **IUPAC** recommendations, it is now written as **u**.
 
 
 
• **Mole (mol):**
 
 
• The **mole** is the **SI unit** of **amount of substance**. One mole contains exactly **6.02214076 x 10^23** elementary entities.
 
• This number is the fixed numerical value of the **Avogadro constant (N_A)**.
 
• The mass of one mole of a substance in grams is called its **molar mass**.
 
 
 
• **Gram (g) and Kilogram (kg):**
 
 
• The **gram** is a metric system unit of mass. It is often used for **molar mass** (expressed as **g/mol**).
 
• The **kilogram** is the **SI base unit** of mass. While **u** is used at the atomic level, **kg** and **g** are used for macroscopic measurements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Molecular Mass and Formula Unit Mass:**

 
 
• **Molecular Mass** is used for compounds that exist as discrete **molecules** (usually **covalent compounds**) like **H2O** or **CH4**.
 
• **Formula Unit Mass** is used for compounds that exist as a 3D network of ions (**ionic compounds**) like **NaCl**, **KNO3**, or **MgO**.
 
• Numerically, both are calculated by summing atomic masses, and both use the unit **u**.
 
 
 
• **History of the Unit:**
 
 
• The **atomic mass unit** was originally defined based on **Hydrogen**, then **Oxygen-16**, before finally settling on **Carbon-12** in the **year 1961** for better precision and stability in measurements across different laboratories worldwide.

questions.question: The making of new cells in organisms is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell division**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell division** is the biological process by which a parent cell divides into two or more **daughter cells**. It is the fundamental mechanism responsible for the **making of new cells** in all living organisms.
 
• In **multicellular organisms**, this process is essential for **growth**, development, and the **repair** or replacement of worn-out or damaged tissues. For example, human skin cells are constantly replaced through this process.
 
• In **unicellular organisms**, cell division is the primary method of **reproduction** (asexual reproduction), where a single cell divides to form two independent organisms.
 
• There are two main types of cell division: **Mitosis**, which results in two daughter cells with the same number of **chromosomes** as the parent, and **Meiosis**, which reduces the chromosome number by half to produce **gametes** (sperm and egg cells).
 
• The importance of this process was summarized by the German physician **Rudolf Virchow** in **1855** with the phrase "**Omnis cellula e cellula**," which translates to "all cells arise from pre-existing cells."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Secretion:** 
 
 
• This is the process by which cells release substances such as **hormones**, **enzymes**, or mucus into the extracellular space.
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** plays a crucial role in packaging these substances into **vesicles** for transport to the cell membrane.
 
 
 
• **Cell Respiration:** 
 
 
• It is a **biochemical process** where cells break down **nutrients** (primarily glucose) to release **energy** in the form of **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**.
 
• In humans, **aerobic respiration** occurs in the **mitochondria** and requires **oxygen** to function efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Cell Fusion:** 
 
 
• This is a process where two or more cells merge their **plasma membranes** and **cytoplasm** to form a single multi-nucleated cell.
 
• Natural examples include **fertilization** (the fusion of a sperm and an egg) and the formation of **muscle fibers**. In biotechnology, it is used to create **hybridomas** for producing monoclonal antibodies.
 
 
 
• **Cell Cycle:** 
 
 
• The life of a cell is organized into a series of stages called the **Cell Cycle**, which includes **Interphase** (growth and DNA replication) and the **M Phase** (Mitosis and Cytokinesis).
 
• Errors in the regulation of the cell cycle can lead to uncontrolled cell division, which is the hallmark of **cancer**.
 
 
</ul

• This formula indicates that for a constant **resistance**, the **power dissipated** increases with the square of the **current**. For example, if the current is doubled, the power dissipation increases **four times**.

questions.question: The Law of Gravitation helped in establishing that:

options.text: the same force governs both falling bodies on Earth and motion of planets
gravitation acts only on terrestrial objects
the Sun revolves around the Earth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the same force governs both falling bodies on Earth and motion of planets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation** established that every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between them.
 
• The law successfully demonstrated that the same force of **gravity** responsible for an object (like an apple) falling to the ground on **Earth** is the same force that keeps the **Moon** in its orbit and the planets in their motion around the **Sun**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The theory proved that **gravitation** is a universal phenomenon and not limited to **terrestrial objects** (objects on Earth). It acts between all bodies having mass, regardless of their location in the universe. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The Law of Gravitation provided the mathematical foundation for the **heliocentric model**, which confirms that planets, including the **Earth**, revolve around the **Sun** due to its massive gravitational pull, rather than the **Sun** revolving around the **Earth**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Gravity acts towards the **center of mass**, which naturally pulls matter into a **spherical shape**. This law helps explain why large celestial bodies like the **Earth** are nearly spherical and certainly not flat. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** **Sir Isaac Newton** formulated this law in **1687** and published it in his landmark work, **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**. This publication is considered one of the most important works in the **history of science**.
 
• **Mathematical Formula:** The force of gravity is expressed as **F = G(m1m2 / r²)**, where **F** is the force, **m1** and **m2** are the masses, **r** is the distance between the centers of the masses, and **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**.
 
• **The Constant G:** The value of the **Gravitational Constant (G)** was later measured with high precision by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**. The current accepted value is approximately **6.674 x 10^-11 N·m²/kg²**.
 
• **Planetary Orbits:** Newton used his law to derive **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion**, proving that planetary orbits are **elliptical** and explaining why planets move faster when they are closer to the **Sun**.
 
• **Ocean Tides:** The law also provides the explanation for **tides** in Earth's oceans, which are caused by the **gravitational attraction** exerted by the **Moon** and the **Sun**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Weakest Fundamental Force:** Despite its universal reach and its ability to hold entire **galaxies** together, **gravity** is the weakest of the **four fundamental forces** of nature (the others being **electromagnetism**, the **strong nuclear force**, and the **weak nuclear force**).
 
• **Infinite Range:** Unlike the nuclear forces which operate only at microscopic distances, **gravitation** has an **infinite range**, although its strength diminishes rapidly as the distance between objects increases (following the **inverse-square law**).
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:** The law clarifies the distinction between **mass** (the amount of matter in an object) and **weight** (the force of gravity acting on that mass). While mass remains **constant**, weight changes depending on the **gravitational field strength** of the planet or moon.
 
• **Center of Gravity:** For calculations involving large bodies like planets, the entire **mass** of the object is treated as if it were concentrated at its **geometric center**, known as the **center of gravity**.

questions.question: What helps flowering plants to grow new plants in the next generation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seed formation and germination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sexual reproduction** in flowering plants, technically called **Angiosperms**, is the process by which they produce offspring for the next generation.
 
• The process begins with **Pollination**, where **Pollen grains** from the **Anther** (male part) are transferred to the **Stigma** (female part).
 
• Following pollination, **Fertilization** occurs when the male gamete fuses with the female gamete in the **Ovule**, leading to the formation of a **Zygote**.
 
• The **Zygote** develops into an **Embryo**, and the **Ovule** matures into a **Seed**. This **Seed** contains the miniature plant of the **next generation**.
 
• **Germination** is the final crucial step where the **Seed**, under favorable conditions like **moisture** and **warmth**, breaks its **dormancy** and begins to grow into a new plant. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **Formation of roots** is a developmental stage of an existing plant or a result of germination; however, roots themselves do not originate the next generation in sexual reproduction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Stigma** is merely a receptive platform for pollen and does not transform into a new individual. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Petals** are accessory organs used to attract insects; they usually fall off after fertilization and do not contribute to the growth of a new plant. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of a Seed:**
 
 
• A **Seed** consists of a **Seed Coat** (protection), **Endosperm** (food storage), and the **Embryo**.
 
• The **Embryo** itself is composed of the **Radicle** (which becomes the primary root) and the **Plumule** (which becomes the shoot).
 
 
 
• **The Process of Germination:**
 
 
• It starts with **Imbibition**, where the seed absorbs **water**, causing it to swell and break the seed coat.
 
• Enzymes are activated to convert stored food into energy for the **Embryo** to grow.
 
• The **Radicle** emerges first to anchor the plant and absorb **nutrients** from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Seeds:**
 
 
• Seeds allow plants to survive unfavorable environmental conditions through a state of **Dormancy**.
 
• They are essential for **Dispersal**, ensuring that the **next generation** of plants can grow in new locations away from the parent plant to avoid competition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Germination:**
 
 
• **Water:** Vital for activating **metabolic** processes.
 
• **Oxygen:** Required for **Aerobic Respiration** to provide energy for growth.
 
• **Temperature:** Most seeds require an optimum **Temperature** range (usually **25-30 degrees Celsius**) to sprout.
 
 
 
• **Types of Seeds:**
 
 
• **Monocotyledonous** (Monocots): Seeds with one **Cotyledon** (e.g., **Maize**, **Rice**).
 
• **Dicotyledonous** (Dicots): Seeds with two **Cotyledons** (e.g., **Gram**, **Pea**).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: If the height of an image ( h' ) is measured perpendicular to and below the principal axis (along the –y-axis), then what sign is assigned to its value according to the convention?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **principal axis** of a spherical mirror or lens is taken as the **X-axis**, and the **pole (P)** or **optical center (O)** is taken as the **origin**.
 
• Heights measured **perpendicular to and above** the principal axis (along the **+y-axis**) are always taken as **positive**. This is generally the case for the **object height (h)**, as objects are usually placed upright.
 
• Heights measured **perpendicular to and below** the principal axis (along the **-y-axis**) are assigned a **negative** sign. ***Hence, the correct answer is Negative.***
 
• This specific convention helps in determining the **nature of the image**. A **negative image height (h')** indicates that the image is **inverted** with respect to the object.
 
• In the case of **real images** formed by **concave mirrors** or **convex lenses**, the image is formed below the principal axis, making its height **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnification (m):** 
 
 
• It is the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**.
 
• Mathematically, **m = h' / h**.
 
• If **magnification is negative**, the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• If **magnification is positive**, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention for Distances:**
 
 
• The **object distance (u)** is always taken as **negative** because the object is always placed to the **left** of the mirror/lens.
 
• The **image distance (v)** is **positive** if the image is formed to the **right** of the origin and **negative** if formed to the **left**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The **focal length** of a **concave mirror** and a **concave lens** is always **negative**.
 
• The **focal length** of a **convex mirror** and a **convex lens** is always **positive**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real and Inverted Images:** For these images, the height **h'** is **negative** because they are formed below the **principal axis**. These are typical for **concave mirrors** (except when the object is between P and F) and **convex lenses** (except when the object is between O and F).
 
• **Virtual and Erect Images:** For these images, the height **h'** is **positive** because they are formed above the **principal axis**. These are always formed by **convex mirrors** and **concave lenses**.
 
• **Origin of Measurement:** All distances parallel to the principal axis are measured from the **pole** of the mirror or the **optical center** of the lens.
 
• **Direction of Incident Light:** Distances measured in the **same direction** as the incident light are taken as **positive**, while those measured **against the direction** of incident light are **negative**.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT true regarding the speed of sound?
(i) Speed of sound increases with the increase in the temperature of the medium.
(ii) Speed of sound in solid state is greater than the speed of sound in gaseous state.
(iii) Speed of sound decreases with the increase in the temperature of the medium.
(iv) Speed of sound is independent of the properties of the medium through which it travels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (iii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Speed of Sound and Temperature:** The **speed of sound** is directly proportional to the **square root** of the **absolute temperature** of the **medium**. When the **temperature** increases, the **kinetic energy** of the **molecules** in the medium increases, allowing the **vibrations** to propagate faster. For every **1 degree Celsius** rise in temperature, the speed of sound in **air** increases by approximately **0.61 meters per second**. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct and statement (iii) is incorrect.***
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different States of Matter:** Sound travels through **elastic media** by the **vibration** of **particles**. In **solids**, the particles are **tightly packed** and the **intermolecular forces** are very strong, which allows sound to travel much faster than in **liquids** or **gases**. In **gases**, the particles are **far apart**, resulting in the lowest speed of sound among the three states. Hence, statement (ii) is correct

questions.question: Which tissue or tissues can help animals respond quickly to changes in their surroundings?

options.text: Nerve impulses and muscle tissue working together
Digestive and excretory systems working together

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nerve impulses and muscle tissue working together**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ability of animals to respond quickly to environmental changes is primarily due to the integrated functioning of the **nervous system** and the **muscular system**.
 
• **Nervous tissue** is composed of specialized cells called **neurons** that are capable of receiving stimuli and transmitting **nerve impulses** (electrochemical signals) at high speeds across the body.
 
• **Muscle tissue** consists of elongated cells, also known as **muscle fibers**, which contain specialized proteins that can contract and relax to produce mechanical movement.
 
• When a change in the **surroundings** (a stimulus) is detected by sensory organs, **nerve impulses** carry this information to the **brain** or **spinal cord**, which then sends a signal back to the muscles to initiate a physical response. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• Bone and cartilage provide structural support and a framework for the body but do not possess the **excitability** or **contractility** required for rapid, active responses to external stimuli. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **muscle tissue** is the effector that performs the movement, it cannot respond to external changes "alone" without the signal provided by the **nervous system**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **digestive** and **excretory systems** are involved in **metabolism**, **nutrient absorption**, and **waste removal**; these processes are relatively slow and are not responsible for immediate behavioral responses to environmental threats or changes. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reflex Arc:**
 
 
• This is the most **rapid response mechanism** in animals. It involves a **sensory neuron**, an **interneuron** in the spinal cord, and a **motor neuron**.
 
• By bypassing the conscious processing of the **brain**, the **reflex arc** allows for near-instantaneous reactions to dangerous stimuli, such as heat or sharp objects.
 
 
 
• **Structure of a Neuron:**
 
 
• A typical neuron consists of a **cell body (cyton)**, **dendrites** (which receive signals), and a long **axon** (which transmits signals).
 
• The **Myelin sheath** acts as an insulator around the axon, significantly increasing the **conduction speed** of nerve impulses through a process called saltatory conduction.
 
 
 
• **Neuromuscular Junction:**
 
 
• This is the specific point of contact where a **motor neuron** meets a **muscle fiber**.
 
• Communication at this junction occurs via a chemical messenger called **acetylcholine**, which triggers the **sliding filament mechanism** of muscle contraction involving **actin** and **myosin** proteins.
 
 
 
• **Types of Muscle Tissue:**
 
 
• **Skeletal Muscle:** Attached to bones and responsible for **voluntary movements**; these are the primary tissues involved in responding to external surroundings.
 
• **Smooth Muscle:** Found in internal organs and responsible for **involuntary movements** like peristalsis.
 
• **Cardiac Muscle:** Found exclusively in the **heart** and responsible for rhythmic pumping of blood.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Homeostasis:** Rapid responses are essential for maintaining **homeostasis**, allowing an organism to adjust its internal state or position to survive environmental fluctuations.
 
• **Sensory Receptors:** These are specialized nerve endings (such as **photoreceptors** for light or **thermoreceptors** for heat) that initiate the **nerve impulse** when they detect specific environmental energy changes.
 
• **Coordination:** The **Central Nervous System (CNS)**, comprising the **brain** and **spinal cord**, acts as the integration center that processes incoming data and coordinates the appropriate muscular output.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following most precisely defines the 'concentration of a solution'?

options.text: The quantity of dissolved substance relative to the solvent
The sensory characteristics such as hue and flavor
The total count of gaseous particles dispersed in air
The proportional relationship between mass and velocity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The quantity of dissolved substance relative to the solvent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concentration of a solution** is defined as the amount of **solute** present in a given quantity of the **solution** or **solvent**. It represents the ratio that determines how "strong" or "weak" a solution is based on the dissolved matter. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct definition.***
 
• A **solute** is the substance that is dissolved (usually present in a smaller amount), while the **solvent** is the medium in which the solute is dissolved (usually present in a larger amount).
 
• The concentration can be expressed qualitatively as **dilute** (low amount of solute) or **concentrated** (high amount of solute), but for scientific precision, it is expressed quantitatively using percentages or molar units.
 
• **Mass by Mass percentage** of a solution is calculated using the formula: (**Mass of solute** / **Mass of solution**) × **100**.
 
• **Mass by Volume percentage** of a solution is calculated as: (**Mass of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**.
 
• Option 2 refers to **physical** or **organoleptic properties** such as color and taste, which may change with concentration but do not define it. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 3 refers to **atmospheric composition** or **gaseous density** rather than a standard liquid solution. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 4 describes **linear momentum** in physics, which is the product of **mass** and **velocity**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Molarity (M)**: This is the most common unit of concentration used in **chemistry**. It is defined as the number of **moles of solute** dissolved in **1 liter** of solution. Its unit is **mol/L**.
 
• **Molality (m)**: This is defined as the number of **moles of solute** per **kilogram (1 kg)** of solvent. Unlike molarity, molality does not change with variations in **temperature** because mass remains constant.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which no more **solute** can be dissolved at a specific **temperature**. Any further addition of solute will result in **precipitation** at the bottom of the container.
 
• **Solubility**: The maximum amount of a **solute** that can be dissolved in **100 grams** of a solvent at a particular **temperature** is called its solubility. Factors affecting solubility include **temperature** and **pressure** (especially for gases).
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: This unit is used to express very low concentrations, such as **pollutants** in water or **trace elements**. It represents one part of solute per **million parts** of the solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Standard Solutions**: In laboratories, a **standard solution** is one whose concentration is accurately known. These are used in **titrations** to determine the concentration of unknown substances.
 
• **Dilution Equation**: When more solvent is added to a solution, the **concentration decreases** but the total moles of solute remain the same. This is expressed by the formula **M1V1 = M2V2**.
 
• **Normality (N)**: Another way to express concentration, specifically in **acid-base chemistry**, representing the number of **equivalent weights** of solute per liter of solution.
 
• **Applications**: Precise concentration measurement is critical in **pharmacology** for medicine dosages, in **food science** for flavor consistency, and in **environmental science** for monitoring **water quality**.

questions.question: When an object is placed beyond the centre of curvature (C) in front of a concave mirror, what kind of image is formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diminished, real, and inverted**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed **beyond the centre of curvature (C)** in front of a **concave mirror**, the reflected rays converge to form an image between the **focus (F)** and the **centre of curvature (C)**.
 
• A ray of light starting from the object and traveling parallel to the **principal axis** passes through the **principal focus (F)** after reflection from the mirror.
 
• Another ray passing through the **centre of curvature (C)** hits the mirror surface perpendicularly and is reflected back along the same path.
 
• The point where these reflected rays intersect is the location of the image. For an object **beyond C**, this intersection occurs in the region **between C and F**.
 
• The characteristics of the image formed in this specific position are **real**, **inverted**, and **diminished** (smaller than the actual size of the object). ***Hence, the correct answer is Diminished, real, and inverted.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror Basics:**
 
 
• A **concave mirror**, also known as a **converging mirror**, has a reflecting surface that is recessed inward (away from the incident light).
 
• It can form both **real** and **virtual** images depending on the distance between the object and the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Image Characteristics at Different Positions:**
 
 
• **At infinity:** The image is formed at the **focus (F)**, is highly **diminished**, **real**, and **inverted**.
 
• **At the centre of curvature (C):** The image is formed at **C**, is of the **same size** as the object, **real**, and **inverted**.
 
• **Between C and F:** The image is formed **beyond C**, is **enlarged**, **real**, and **inverted**.
 
• **At the focus (F):** The image is formed at **infinity**, is highly **enlarged**, **real**, and **inverted**.
 
• **Between the pole (P) and focus (F):** The image is formed **behind the mirror**, is **enlarged**, **virtual**, and **upright** (erect).
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Real Image:** An image that is formed when light rays actually meet at a point after reflection; it can be projected onto a **screen**.
 
• **Virtual Image:** An image that appears to be formed at a point where light rays do not actually meet but only appear to diverge from; it cannot be caught on a **screen**.
 
• **Centre of Curvature (C):** The center of the hollow glass sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• **Principal Axis:** The straight line passing through the **pole (P)** and the **centre of curvature (C)** of the spherical mirror.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** are used in **shaving mirrors** and **makeup mirrors** to see an enlarged image of the face.
 
• They are used by **dentists** to see large images of the teeth of patients.
 
• They are also used as reflectors in **torches**, **vehicle headlights**, and **searchlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The focal length (f) of a concave mirror is always **negative** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**, as it is measured in the direction opposite to the incident light.
 
• The relation between the **radius of curvature (R)** and the **focal length (f)** is given by **R = 2f**.
 
• In the case of an object **beyond C**, the **magnification (m)** is **negative** and its absolute value is **less than 1**, signifying a real, inverted, and diminished image.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is not an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Microbes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ecosystem** is a functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and with the surrounding physical environment. It consists of two major components: **Biotic** and **Abiotic**.
 
• **Abiotic components** comprise the non-living physical and chemical elements in the environment. These include **Temperature**, **Rainfall**, **Wind**, **Light**, **Soil**, and **Humidity**.
 
• **Temperature** is a crucial abiotic factor that affects the kinetics of enzymes and through it the metabolic activity and other physiological functions of the organism. ***Hence, it is an abiotic component.***
 
• **Rainfall** (Precipitation) and **Wind** are climatic abiotic factors. Rainfall determines the availability of **water**, which is essential for life, while wind affects **transpiration** and **pollination**. ***Hence, these are abiotic components.***
 
• **Microbes**, such as **Bacteria** and **Fungi**, are living organisms. In an ecosystem, they serve as **Decomposers** or **Saprophytes**, breaking down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances.
 
• Because **Microbes** are living entities, they are classified as **Biotic components**, not abiotic. ***Hence, the statement that Microbes are not an abiotic component is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biotic Components:**
 
 
• These include all living beings in an **ecosystem**. They are categorized based on their functional roles into **Producers** (Autotrophs like green plants), **Consumers** (Heterotrophs like animals), and **Decomposers** (Microbes).
 
• **Producers** fix solar energy via **photosynthesis**, while **Consumers** depend on producers for food. **Decomposers** recycle nutrients back into the **soil**, completing the nutrient cycle.
 
 
 
• **Abiotic Components Classification:**
 
 
• **Climatic Factors:** These include **light**, **temperature**, **water**, **wind**, and **humidity** which define the physical environment.
 
• **Edaphic Factors:** These relate to the **soil**, including **soil texture**, **pH**, **minerals**, and **topography**.
 
• **Inorganic Substances:** Elements like **Carbon**, **Nitrogen**, **Hydrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Sulphur** that cycle within the ecosystem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Temperature:**
 
 
• It is the most ecologically relevant environmental factor. The average temperature on land varies **seasonally** and decreases progressively from the **equator** towards the **poles** and from **plains** to the **mountain tops**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Water:**
 
 
• Life on **Earth** originated in water and is unsustainable without it. For aquatic organisms, the quality (chemical composition, **pH**) of water becomes more important than just its presence.
 
 
 
• **Role of Light:**
 
 
• Since plants produce food through **photosynthesis**, a process which is only possible when **sunlight** is available as a source of energy, light is a critical abiotic factor for the survival of the entire **biotic community**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: During uniform motion of an object along a straight line __________.

options.text: The change in velocity over any time interval is zero.
The change in velocity over any time interval is non zero.
The velocity has different values at different instants and at different points of the path.
The velocity changes continuously with time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The change in velocity over any time interval is zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uniform Motion** is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels in a **straight line** and covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, regardless of the duration of the time interval.
 
• In this type of motion, the **magnitude** of the **velocity** (speed) and the **direction** of motion remain **constant** throughout the entire duration of the journey.
 
• The **change in velocity** (represented as Δv) is calculated by subtracting the initial velocity from the final velocity. Since the velocity is constant at every **instant** of time in uniform motion, the difference is always **zero**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• If the change in velocity over any time interval were **non-zero**, it would imply that the object is either speeding up or slowing down, which characterizes **non-uniform** or **accelerated motion**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

questions.question: The reaction of an alcohol with ethanoic acid in the presence of a catalyst forms water and:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An ester**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between an **alcohol** and a **carboxylic acid** (such as **ethanoic acid**) in the presence of an **acid catalyst** is known as **Esterification**.
 
• When **ethanoic acid** reacts with an alcohol like **ethanol**, it produces a sweet-smelling substance called an **ester** along with **water**. ***Hence, the correct answer is An ester.***
 
• The catalyst commonly used in this process is **concentrated sulfuric acid** (**H2SO4**), which acts as both a **catalyst** and a **dehydrating agent** to remove the water formed during the reaction.
 
• The general chemical equation for this specific reaction using **ethanol** is: **CH3COOH** (Ethanoic acid) + **C2H5OH** (Ethanol) → **CH3COOC2H5** (Ethyl ethanoate) + **H2O** (Water).
 
• **Esters** are characterized by the functional group **-COOR**, where **R** is an **alkyl** or **aryl group**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics and Uses of Esters**:
 
 
• **Esters** are generally **volatile liquids** with **pleasant, fruity smells**.
 
• Because of their fragrance, they are widely used in the **perfume industry**, **cosmetics**, and as **artificial flavoring agents** in the **food industry** (e.g., to mimic the smell of **apples**, **bananas**, or **pineapples**).
 
• They also serve as excellent **organic solvents** for **lacquers**, **varnishes**, and **plastics**.
 
 
 
• **Saponification**:
 
 
• This is the **reverse reaction** of esterification, where an **ester** reacts with a **base** (like **Sodium Hydroxide** or **NaOH**) to produce **alcohol** and the **sodium salt** of the carboxylic acid.
 
• This process is primarily used in the **manufacturing of soaps**.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Aldehydes**: These are formed by the **oxidation** of primary alcohols using oxidizing agents like **acidified potassium dichromate** (**K2Cr2O7**) or **PCC**, not by reaction with organic acids.
 
• **Hydrocarbons**: Alcohols can be converted into **hydrocarbons** (specifically **alkenes**) through **dehydration**. For example, heating **ethanol** at **443 K** with **excess concentrated sulfuric acid** yields **ethene**.
 
• **Salts**: Alcohols react with **active metals** like **Sodium** (**Na**) to form **alkoxides** (which are **salts**) and release **hydrogen gas**. Example: **2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fischer Esterification**: This is the formal **name** given to the **acid-catalyzed** reaction between a **carboxylic acid** and an **alcohol**. It was discovered by **Emil Fischer** in the **year 1895**.
 
• **Equilibrium**: The esterification reaction is **reversible**. To shift the **equilibrium** toward the product (ester), **water** is often removed as it forms, or an **excess** of one of the **reactants** is used.
 
• **Reactivity**: The **rate of reaction** depends on the **steric hindrance** of the alcohol and the acid. **Primary alcohols** react faster than **secondary** and **tertiary alcohols** in this **chemical process**.
</ul

questions.question: Bleaching powder is chemically formed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ca(OH)₂ reacting with Cl₂ gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bleaching powder** is chemically known as **Calcium oxychloride** or **Chloride of lime**. Its chemical formula is represented as **CaOCl₂**, though the actual composition is quite complex.
 
• It is produced by the action of **chlorine gas** (**Cl₂**) on **dry slaked lime** [**Ca(OH)₂**]. This reaction is the standard industrial method for manufacturing bleaching powder. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The chemical equation for the formation is: **Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O**. In this process, **calcium hydroxide** reacts with **chlorine** to yield the bleaching agent and **water**.
 
• The reaction between **Calcium chloride** (**CaCl₂**) and **Oxygen** (**O₂**) does not result in the formation of bleaching powder. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction between **Calcium carbonate** (**CaCO₃**) and **Carbon dioxide** (**CO₂**) usually relates to the formation of calcium bicarbonate in the presence of water but not bleaching powder. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction between **Sodium hydroxide** (**NaOH**) and **Hydrochloric acid** (**HCl**) is a classic **neutralization reaction** that produces **Sodium chloride** (**NaCl**) and **water**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Uses:** **Bleaching powder** is extensively used in the **textile industry** for **bleaching cotton and linen** and in the **paper industry** for **bleaching wood pulp**. It is also used for **bleaching washed clothes** in **laundry**.
 
• **Disinfectant and Water Treatment:** It serves as a powerful **disinfectant** and **germicide**. It is commonly used to **sterilize drinking water** supplies by killing harmful **bacteria** and **pathogens**.
 
• **Chemical Oxidizing Agent:** Due to its ability to release **nascent oxygen**, it is utilized as an **oxidizing agent** in various **chemical industries** and laboratories.
 
• **Manufacturing Chloroform:** In chemical synthesis, bleaching powder is used in the **production of chloroform** (**CHCl₃**).
 
• **Physical Properties:** It is a **pale yellowish powder** that gives off a **strong smell of chlorine**. It is **soluble in cold water**, although a small portion (lime) often remains as an insoluble residue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Available Chlorine:** The efficiency of bleaching powder is measured by the percentage of **available chlorine**, which is the chlorine liberated when it reacts with **dilute acids**. Good quality commercial bleaching powder contains about **33% to 38%** available chlorine.
 
• **Storage Conditions:** It must be stored in **air-tight containers** because when exposed to air, it reacts with **carbon dioxide** (**CO₂**) to release **chlorine gas**, thereby losing its strength over time.
 
• **Reaction Temperature:** For the effective production of bleaching powder, the **dry slaked lime** is treated with **chlorine gas** at a temperature of approximately **40 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **History:** The process of creating bleaching powder was first patented by **Charles Tennant** in the **year 1799**, which revolutionized the **textile industry** by significantly reducing the time required for bleaching fabrics.
</ul

questions.question: What is rancidity?

options.text: The process of preserving food by adding salt or sugar
The process of food becoming stale due to drying
The process of food decaying due to bacterial growth
The process where fats and oils in food are oxidised, leading to changes in smell and taste

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The process where fats and oils in food are oxidised, leading to changes in smell and taste**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rancidity** refers to the condition produced by the **aerial oxidation** of **unsaturated fats** and **oils** present in foods, which results in an unpleasant **odour** and **flavour**.
 
• When fats and oils are exposed to **oxygen**, they undergo a chemical reaction that breaks down the long-chain **fatty acids** into smaller, volatile compounds like **aldehydes** and **ketones**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The process of preserving food by adding **salt** or **sugar** is known as **curing** or **osmotic dehydration**, which inhibits microbial growth by reducing water activity. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The process of food becoming stale specifically due to **drying** is called **desiccation** or **moisture loss**, which is distinct from the chemical oxidation of lipids. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The decay of food caused by **bacterial growth**, **fungi**, or **enzymatic action** is generally termed **food spoilage** or **putrefaction**, which involves the breakdown of **proteins** and **carbohydrates** alongside lipids. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Rancidity:**
 
 
• **Oxidative Rancidity:** This occurs when **oxygen** from the air reacts with the **double bonds** of **unsaturated fatty acids**. It is accelerated by **light**, **heat**, and **metal catalysts** like **iron** or **copper**.
 
• **Hydrolytic Rancidity:** This happens when **water** splits fatty acid chains away from the **glycerol** backbone in **triglycerides**, often facilitated by **enzymes** called **lipases**. This is common in **butter** and **dairy products**.
 
• **Microbial Rancidity:** Occurs when **microorganisms** like **bacteria** or **moulds** use their enzymes to break down chemical structures in fats.
 
 
 
• **Prevention Methods:**
 
 
• **Antioxidants:** Adding substances like **BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole)** and **BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene)** prevents the **oxidation** chain reaction.
 
• **Inert Gas Packaging:** Food items like **potato chips** are flushed with **Nitrogen gas** to displace **oxygen** and prevent rancidity.
 
• **Vacuum Packing:** Removing air entirely from the container limits the availability of **oxygen** for the reaction.
 
• **Refrigeration:** Lowering the **temperature** slows down the rate of chemical reactions and **enzymatic** activity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unsaturated fats**, particularly **Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids (PUFAs)** found in vegetable oils, are significantly more susceptible to rancidity than **saturated fats** because of the presence of **carbon-carbon double bonds**.
 
• **Rancid food** is not only unpalatable but can also lead to the loss of **nutritional value**, especially the destruction of **fat-soluble vitamins** like **Vitamin A** and **Vitamin E**.
 
• In the **food industry**, the **Peroxide Value (PV)** is a standard **analytical test** used to measure the extent of **oxidative rancidity** in oils and fats.
 
• Storing food in **dark-coloured glass** or **opaque containers** helps prevent **Photo-oxidation**, which is rancidity triggered by **UV light**.
</ul

__

This reaction demonstrates the **acidic nature** of alcohols, as they donate a proton (H+) to the metal. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Statement B**: **Ethanol** (C2H5OH) is a primary alcohol that reacts vigorously with **metallic sodium**. When a small piece of **sodium** is added to **ethanol**, it results in the formation of **sodium ethoxide** and the evolution of **hydrogen gas**, which can be observed as **brisk effervescence** or bubbles. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• The general chemical equation for the reaction between an alcohol and **sodium** is: **2R-OH + 2Na -> 2R-ONa + H2**. For **ethanol**, the specific reaction is: **2CH3CH2OH + 2Na -> 2CH3CH2ONa + H2**.
 
• The evolution of **hydrogen gas** in this reaction is often used as a **confirmatory test** in laboratories to identify the presence of the **alcoholic functional group** in an organic compound.
 
• The rate of reaction depends on the type of alcohol; **primary alcohols** like **ethanol** react faster with **sodium** compared to **secondary** or **tertiary alcohols** due to steric hindrance and the inductive effect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acidity of Alcohols**:
 
 
• Alcohols are **weak acids**, even weaker than **water** (with the exception of **methanol**). The **acidic strength** of alcohols follows the order: **Primary > Secondary > Tertiary**.
 
• The **alkoxide ion** (R-O-) formed after the release of a proton is a **strong conjugate base**, making **sodium ethoxide** a useful reagent in **organic synthesis** and **dehydrohalogenation** reactions.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Ethanol**:
 
 
• **Ethanol**, also known as **ethyl alcohol** or **grain alcohol**, is a colorless, volatile liquid with a characteristic odor. It has a boiling point of **78.37 degrees Celsius**.
 
• It is widely used as a **solvent**, in the manufacture of **pharmaceuticals**, **perfumes**, and as a **biofuel** component (often blended with **petrol** at **10% to 20%** levels).
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Laboratory Uses**:
 
 
• The reaction of **sodium** with **ethanol** is used to produce **sodium ethoxide**, which acts as a **catalyst** in various chemical reactions like the **Claisen condensation**.
 
• In the **year 1834**, the concept of **functional groups** helped chemists understand why different alcohols exhibit similar **chemical properties**, such as the reaction with **alkali metals**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Safety Precautions**: The reaction between **sodium** and **ethanol** is **exothermic** (releases heat). **Sodium metal** is highly reactive and must be stored under **kerosene** or **paraffin oil** to prevent reaction with **atmospheric moisture**.
 
• **Comparison with Water**: When **sodium** reacts with **water**, the reaction is much more **violent** and **explosive** compared to its reaction with **ethanol**, although both produce **hydrogen gas**.
 
• **Identification**: To confirm the gas evolved is **hydrogen**, a burning splinter can be brought near the mouth of the test tube, which will extinguish with a **"pop" sound**.

questions.question: A force of 10 { N} acts on a body of mass 2 { kg} . The acceleration produced is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m/s²**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The fundamental principle used to solve this problem is **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which describes the relationship between an object's mass and the amount of force needed to accelerate it. 
• According to this law, the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the net **force** acting upon it and inversely proportional to its **mass**. 
• The mathematical formula for this relationship is **F = m × a**, where **F** represents the net force in **Newtons (N)**, **m** represents the mass in **kilograms (kg)**, and **a** represents the acceleration in **meters per second squared (m/s²)**. 
• In the given question, the **Force (F)** acting on the body is **10 N** and the **Mass (m)** of the body is **2 kg**. 
• To find the acceleration, we rearrange the formula to **a = F / m**. Substituting the provided numerical values: **a = 10 N / 2 kg**. 
• The calculation yields **5 m/s²**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 5 m/s².*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Force (F)**: 
• It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**. 
• **1 Newton** is defined as the force that produces an acceleration of **1 m/s²** in a body of mass **1 kg**. 
• **Mass (m)**: 
• It is a **scalar quantity** and is a measure of the amount of matter in an object. Its **SI unit** is the **kilogram (kg)**. 
• Mass is also a quantitative measure of **inertia**, which is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity. 
• **Acceleration (a)**: 
• Acceleration is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to time. It is a **vector quantity**. 
• The direction of acceleration is always in the direction of the **net external force** acting on the object. 
• **Interdependence of Variables**: 
• If the **mass** is kept constant, doubling the **force** will result in doubling the **acceleration**. 
• Conversely, if the **force** is kept constant, doubling the **mass** will result in halving the **acceleration**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion**: 
• **First Law (Law of Inertia)**: An object will remain at rest or move at a constant velocity unless acted upon by an external **force**. 
• **Third Law**: For every action, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. This means forces always exist in pairs. 
• **Practical Applications**: 
• The formula **F = ma** is used extensively in engineering and physics, from calculating the thrust needed for a **rocket** to launch to determining the braking force required for a **car**. 
• In **space exploration**, understanding these ratios is crucial because **mass** remains constant, but the **weight** (force due to gravity) changes depending on the celestial body. 
• **Dimensional Analysis**: 
• The dimensions of force are **[MLT⁻²]**. This is derived from the product of mass **[M]** and acceleration **[LT⁻²]**.
